# Computer science fundamentals and resources

## Why This Matters

Computing skills are the practical engine of bioinformatics. These fundamentals let you run analyses, collaborate, and reproduce your results.

## Learning Outcomes

- Work comfortably in Linux command line environments.
- Use Git/GitHub for collaboration and version control.
- Write and run small scripts in Python and R.
- Organize project files so work is reproducible.

## Suggested Time

- **Minimum**: 3 weeks (core usage)
- **Recommended**: 4-6 weeks (with mini projects)

## Linux Fundamentals

### Key Concepts

- File system navigation and permissions
- Shell commands and pipes
- Simple shell scripting for automation
- Package and environment management

### Recommended Resources

- **Books**:
  - *The Linux Command Line* by William Shotts

- **Online Courses and Tutorials**:
  - [HPC Carpentry: Introduction to Linux](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/hpc-intro/)
  - [MIT Missing Semester (Shell)](https://missing.csail.mit.edu/)

## Version Control: Git and GitHub

### Why It Matters

Git helps you track changes, collaborate safely, and recover from mistakes without losing your work history.

### Core Concepts

- **Repository**: your tracked project folder
- **Commit**: a saved checkpoint
- **Branch**: an isolated line of work
- **Pull Request**: proposed changes for review

### Quick Command Workflow

```bash
# Clone project and create a feature branch
git clone https://github.com/username/repository.git
cd repository
git checkout -b feature/your-topic

# Work, commit, and push
git status
git add .
git commit -m "Add your update"
git pull --rebase
git push -u origin feature/your-topic
```

### Beginner-Safe Recovery Patterns

```bash
# Unstage a file (keep edits)
git restore --staged path/to/file

# Discard local edits in one file
git restore path/to/file

# Revert a bad commit with a new safe commit
git revert <commit_hash>

# Temporarily save unfinished work
git stash push -m "wip: notes"
git stash pop
```

Avoid destructive commands (for example `git reset --hard`) unless you fully understand the impact.

## Programming Foundations: Python and R

### Python

- **Use cases**: data wrangling, automation, analysis pipelines, ML
- **Start with**:
  - *Python for Biologists* by Martin Jones
  - [Python for Data Science and AI](https://www.coursera.org/learn/python-for-applied-data-science-ai)

### R

- **Use cases**: statistics, visualization, transcriptomics workflows
- **Start with**:
  - *R for Data Science* by Hadley Wickham
  - [R Programming](https://www.coursera.org/learn/r-programming)

## Mini Project

<details>
<summary>Build one reproducible starter project</summary>

- Create a GitHub repo with `README.md`.
- Add one Python or R script that loads and summarizes a public dataset.
- Save output table/plot in `results/`.
- Share the repo link with a short method summary.

</details>
